display.title: Episode 291: The Sound of the Shofar (Elul)
display.summary_short: An Elul show: pressing the 'total button' on the year's mitzvos, Shema with a visiting first-grade class, and the parable of the village that blew a bugle to put out a fire.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the first week of Elul 5747. Uncle Yossi compares Elul to pressing the 'total' button on a calculator: we add up the year's mitzvos, resolve not to repeat our aveiros, and Hashem erases them so only good deeds remain before Rosh Hashanah. Recalling the Alter Rebbe's parable of the King in the field, he calls Elul the days of goodwill, when we should 'smile back' at Hashem. After the Hakochainik march, a first-grade class from a Brooklyn yeshiva recites the Shema. Story time explains the shofar: the Torah gives no reason, but the Rambam teaches that it is an alarm to wake us. In the parable, villagers plagued by fires send a farm boy to the big city, where he sees the fire chief blow a bugle from a tower; back home he blows with all his might while the houses burn, until the chief explains that the bugle only calls people to fetch water. So too the shofar calls us to act with teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah. The show ends with a bar mitzvah wish and a reminder to mail in mitzvah charts.
display.lesson: The shofar is an alarm, not the cure: it calls us to act, with teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah.
